name: Standard NAFNet (no distillation)
mechanism: Train NAFNet directly on the restoration task with no teacher signal at all
key_assumption: No degradation-aware teacher signal is needed for adequate quality
advantages: Simplest, no teacher dependency, fastest to implement, no distillation-alignment risk
risks: May underperform vs. any teacher-guided variant on hard/ambiguous degradations; forgoes AdaIR's demonstrated degradation-discriminative signal for free
what_test06_must_test: Whether teacher-guided variants actually beat this baseline by a meaningful margin, not just in classification accuracy but in restoration PSNR/SSIM/perceptual quality

name: NAFNet + conventional feature distillation
mechanism: Match NAFNet intermediate features to AdaIR intermediate features (e.g. L2/cosine loss on matched-resolution feature maps)
key_assumption: Direct feature matching transfers useful information even without explicit degradation conditioning
supported_by_test05_5: Indirectly supported -- z_T (AdaIR's raw features) is confirmed rich/discriminative (Claim A/D)
advantages: Simple, well-established distillation recipe, no new architecture needed on the student side
risks: Feature-matching losses can fight the student's own capacity/architecture; does not explicitly leverage the compact degradation-embedding finding (Claim E) or address why a smaller e_D might generalize better
what_test06_must_test: Whether raw feature matching transfers degradation-adaptive behavior at all, or just generic restoration quality (i.e. does it beat model A)

name: NAFNet + compact latent distillation
mechanism: Distill only the compact embedding e_D (PCA-16-style projection of z_T), not the full feature map, via an auxiliary loss or conditioning signal
key_assumption: A 16-dim compact code retains the useful degradation information at much lower transfer/compute cost
supported_by_test05_5: STRONGLY SUPPORTED by TEST05.5 -- PCA-16 is leakage-safe validated (Claim E), beats random projection, degradation-relevant (R^2=0.67-0.68 for restoration PSNR)
advantages: Small transfer footprint (NPU-friendly, the project's stated goal), empirically validated compactness, negative controls confirm it isn't a dimensionality artifact
risks: Whether a LEARNED (not PCA) 16-dim projection trained end-to-end with the student performs as well as the post-hoc PCA analysis suggests; whether 16 dims remains sufficient once restoration (not just classification) is the actual training objective
what_test06_must_test: Does a NAFNet student conditioned on a 16-dim compact code reach competitive PSNR/SSIM vs. models A/B, and does the learned code stay leakage-safe/scene-robust under end-to-end training

name: NAFNet + explicit degradation embedding (classifier-style, degradation-ID conditioning)
mechanism: Predict an explicit (soft) degradation class/embedding from the input and use it to condition NAFNet (e.g. FiLM-style), independent of AdaIR's internal features
key_assumption: An explicit degradation signal, even a simple classifier-derived one, is sufficient to condition restoration -- doesn't require distilling AdaIR's internals at all
supported_by_test05_5: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED, and with a significant caveat: Phase 1 shows simple pixel statistics ALONE reach 99% degradation accuracy on the easy dataset -- an explicit degradation classifier may need only cheap hand-crafted or lightweight-CNN features, not AdaIR distillation at all
advantages: Cheapest of all teacher-dependent options if a lightweight classifier suffices (Phase 1 suggests it might, on datasets resembling TEST03); no dependency on AdaIR whatsoever at deployment time
risks: Phase 3-4 shows AdaIR's advantage over simple stats emerges specifically on the HARDER randomized-severity dataset (99.7% vs 68.8%) -- a simple classifier may not generalize as well to real-world degradation variability; conflates 'useful signal' with 'discrete degradation label', which may lose continuous severity information
what_test06_must_test: Whether a cheap standalone degradation classifier (no AdaIR) generalizes to real-world degradation variability as well as AdaIR-derived compact embeddings do, especially under severity/parameter shift

name: Frequency-aware teacher -> compact embedding -> spatial modulation (the ORIGINAL F2S hypothesis as specified)
mechanism: Use AdaIR's frequency-domain processing specifically as the source of e_D, then modulate student kernels spatially
key_assumption: The frequency-domain computation inside AdaIR is what makes its representation degradation-aware
supported_by_test05_5: CONTRADICTED by TEST05.5 Phase 7-9/10 -- the frequency branch is causally inert for both output quality and representation quality at this benchmark resolution (degenerate mask, h_=w_=0)
advantages: None specific to this design beyond what Model C already offers; the 'frequency' framing does not add anything demonstrated by this audit
risks: Building explicit machinery to distill 'frequency-derived' information that TEST05.5 shows is not meaningfully frequency-derived in the first place -- wasted engineering effort and a misleading name for the mechanism actually being distilled
what_test06_must_test: N/A -- audit result argues this specific mechanism should not proceed as conceived unless a HIGHER-resolution regime is tested where AdaIR's learned mask is no longer degenerate (see report Limitations)

name: Frequency-aware teacher -> dynamic/low-rank spatial kernels (same as E but with the K_D=K_0+sum a_r K_r kernel-bank formulation)
mechanism: Same frequency-causality assumption as E, plus an additional unverified claim that the kernel-bank G_phi/K_D machinery is learnable and beneficial
key_assumption: Same frequency-domain dependency assumption as E
supported_by_test05_5: Same CONTRADICTED status as E for the frequency-dependency assumption; the kernel-bank mechanism itself (G_phi, K_D) is simply UNTESTED (not contradicted, just never evaluated) since it's a student-side architecture question TEST05.5 was scoped to avoid
advantages: If e_D were swapped for a non-frequency-specific compact code (i.e. hybridized with Model C), the kernel-bank idea itself remains an open, untested, architecturally interesting mechanism
risks: Inherits E's core flaw (frequency framing not justified) AND adds unverified complexity (dynamic low-rank kernels) on top; highest implementation risk of all 6 options for the least-justified benefit
what_test06_must_test: If pursued at all, should be decoupled from the frequency-specific framing and tested as 'Model C's compact code -> dynamic kernel bank' -- i.e., G_phi/K_D's value as an architecture, independent of e_D's frequency provenance
